The final portfolio must contain at least five well-supported stories in every category. Treat social attention as a discovery signal rather than verification. More than half of the final stories must originate with independent, local or social discovery, using the first source in each story as the discovery source; established outlets may account for no more than half.

items.title: Allahabad HC asks State to enhance compensation for dependents of advocates under financial aid scheme
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court has directed the State government to consider enhancing the amount of compensation payable to the dependents of deceased advocates [ Jyotima v State of UP and 2 Others ]. A Division Bench of Justice Ajit Kumar and Justice Garima Prashad noted that the compensation under the ‘Financial Assistance Scheme for Advocates’ was fixed at ₹5 lakh in 2015 and since then, the corpus for the scheme has swollen to ₹330 crore from ₹20 crore. However, the Court observed that the compensation amount has remained static at ₹5 lakh. It thus called upon the government to consider increasing the compensation amount. “Let the Government come up with an affidavit as to what amount it proposes to enhance towards the compensation under financial assistance scheme, and we leave it to the wisdom of the State Government. If a proper affidavit in this regard is not filed by the next date fixed, this Court will be compelled to take a serious view of the matter,” the Court directed. items.title: Even 0.1% of amount spent for Nashik Kumbh Mela could save Marathi medium schools: Supreme Court Justice PB Varale
items.summary: Supreme Court Justice Prasanna B Varale recently raised serious concerns over the declining budget for education in Maharashtra, contrasting the closure of State-run Marathi medium schools with the massive public expenditure on events like the Nashik-Trimbakeshwar Simhastha or Nashik Kumbh Mela. The judge was speaking at an event organised by a high school in Dhule district of Maharashtra, where he had been a student for a few years. The event was an inauguration of 'smart classes'. He referred to recent announcements regarding government expenditure on the Nashik-Trimbakeshwar Simhastha Kumbh Mela and major infrastructure corridors. “The government claims to allocate vast funds for various initiatives. The Deputy Chief Minister mentioned ₹32,000 crore and the Chief Minister mentioned ₹34,000 crore for the Kumbh Mela. I read elsewhere about ₹11,000 crore being allocated for a corridor project,” Justice Varale pointed out. items.title: AP: Rifle coach accused of murder, suicide and forced conversion arrested
items.summary: The Andhra Pradesh police have arrested rifle shooting coach Sheikh Sadiq Khan on charges of murder, abetment of suicide and insulting religious beliefs in connection with the deaths of a woman, Soujanya, her husband and her parents. On August 16, Soujanya, her mother Meena and her father K Nooka Raju, an Assistant Engineer with the Panchayat Raj Department in Pithapuram, died by suicide in Rajahmundry. Soujanya’s 10-year-old son, Reyansh, who survived the suicide attempt, told the police that Sadiq, his rifle shooting coach, had allegedly been threatening and extorting his family. Later, Soujanya’s father-in-law found a suicide note purportedly written by her. In the note, she alleged that Sadiq had killed her husband, Jagadeeshwara Reddy, in July, and had subsequently threatened and tortured her, exercised control over her family’s property, and forced her to read books related to Islam and convert to Islam. Two separate cases were registered against Sadiq on August 17. The first was registered at the Rajahmundry II Town police station for allegedly abetting the suicides of Soujanya and her parents. items.summary: The Allahabad High Court recently rejected a Muslim student’s plea seeking directions to allow her to wear a (hijab) headscarf in addition to the uniform prescribed by her school [Sukaina Rizvi v State of UP and Others] In a judgment delivered on August 21, a bench of Justice JJ Munir and Justice Indrajeet Shukla noted that High Courts have been unanimous in their opinion that wearing a headscarf is not essential part of the Islamic faith for a woman. Pertinently, the Court also said that Karnataka High Court’s decision against wearing of hijabs in schools continues to hold the field as the Supreme Court is yet to settle the dispute after a split verdict “In view of the difference of opinion, the matter was directed to be placed before the Hon’ble the Chief Justice for the constitution of an appropriate Bench. There is no authoritative pronouncement as yet by the Supreme Court, finally settling the issue, arising from the judgment of the Karnataka Full Bench. We are of opinion that the Karnataka Full Bench, like the other Courts, is nevertheless persuasive authority of great value and there is no reason for us to take a different view,” it noted. items.title: CBSE OSM row: Supreme Court refuses to direct reopening of re-evaluation portal for class XII answer sheets
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday refused to direct the reopening of the CBSE Class XII examination verification and re-evaluation portal for students with grievances over the evaluation of their answer sheets through the On-Screen Marking (OSM) system. A Bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana observed the portal had already been opened for all candidates for a specified period and that reopening it could trigger lakhs of fresh claims. "If you don't use the bus, you miss the bus," CJI Kant said. Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana The Court was hearing a petition challenging the manner in which CBSE introduced the OSM system for evaluation of answer sheets. The plea pointed out that OSM was implemented for the first time in 2026 and that teachers were not provided formal training before its implementation. The plea alleged that the introduction of digital scanning resulted in several irregularities, including certain pages of answer sheets not being scanned, illegible scans and answers or pages not being evaluated. items.title: Delhi HC directs State to decide public prosecutors' challenge to biometric attendance system
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Monday directed the Delhi government to decide within four weeks the public prosecutors’ plea challenging Aadhaar based biometric attendance system [ Delhi Prosecutors Welfare Association Vs State GNCT of Delhi and Anr ]. Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma passed the directions on August 17 while considering a petition filed by Delhi Prosecutors Welfare Association seeking quashing of Delhi government’s circulars requiring recording of biometric attendance of public prosecutors. Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma The petitioner-association challenged two circulars mandating the implementation of Aadhaar Enabled Biometric Attendance System (AEBAS) for public prosecutors. The association submitted that public prosecutors, being officers of the court, are required to visit different courts, police stations and other locations while discharging their duties. The biometric system is impractical and the presence of prosecutors is reflected in the court records and proceedings, it was contended. Biometric attendance was implemented without taking into account their previous representation to the government challenging the mechanism, it was submitted. The association alternativ

items.title: Allahabad High Court takes serious note of IAS officer's alleged attempt to influence trial judge
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court recently expressed concern over allegations that senior Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer Durga Shakti Nagpal had attempted to pressure a trial judge through a phone call in connection with a long-pending land case [ Jyoti Vidya Mandir v Nagar Palika Parishad & Ors. ]. In a letter to the district judge, the civil judge alleged that the IAS officer attempted to exert pressure on her during a phone conversation by questioning her about her leave and seeking to discuss a pending case. The IAS officer has maintained that she had not tried to discuss the merits of the case, and had only sought to know when the judge would resume hearing the matter. On August 21, Justice Syed Qamar Hasan Rizvi of the High Court took a serious view of the allegations against the IAS officer. "The tone and language of the aforesaid alleged telephonic conversation given a direct impression that the Presiding Officer of the Court was tried to be influenced and that made her feel offended ... It is shocking that how a litigating party can approach the Court by making such a phone call and that too in context with a pending matter before the said Court ," observed the Court.

In a press release issued on August 24, KSBC nominated Chairman Kamaraddi VD said, "While the newly elected members of the KSBC await the formal takeover of office as per BCI guidelines, myself the Chairman, as the administrator of the Karnataka State Bar Council, reiterates absolute faith and confidence in favor of Shri Manan Kumar Mishra leading the Bar Council of India." Kamaraddi Venkaraddi Devaraddi YR Sadasiva Reddy had called for Mishra's resignation on the grounds that the BCI's August 13 direction (later withdrawn) to bar NALSAR graduating students from enrolment as advocates was issued without the Council's deliberation, resolution or authorisation. items.title: Supreme Court to hear tomorrow FIR quashing plea by journalist Abhishek Upadhyay who reported on Ram Mandir donation theft
items.summary: Journalist Abhishek Upadhyay, who reported about Ram Mandir donation theft in Ayodhya, has approached the Supreme Court to quash the first information report (FIR) lodged against him in a road rage case. He has alleged that the road rage case, which invokes provisions under the stringent, SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, was a counter blast to target him for his investigative reports on the Ram Mandir Trust and alleged corruption in the Uttar Pradesh administration. The matter was mentioned before a bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana which agreed to the list the matter tomorrow (August 25). "Multiple FIRs have been filed against him and now an FIR under the stringent provisions of the SC/ST Act has also been filed. The police party raided his house on the 20th. Yesterday also, the police came at 5 o'clock. I have filed my writ petition. I request that it may be listed today or tomorrow, whatever is possible," the counsel said. items.title: Bengaluru parking fee should not burden residents, says Minister Ramalinga Reddy
items.summary: Forest, Ecology and Environment Minister Ramalinga Reddy has asked Chief Minister DK Shivakumar to reconsider the proposed annual fee of Rs 15,000 to Rs 25,000 for residential roadside parking in Bengaluru, warning that the charge could put an additional financial burden on middle-class households. In a letter to Shivakumar, Reddy acknowledged the need to crack down on illegal and prolonged parking on city streets, but said the proposed fee should take into account residents who have no alternative parking space within their homes. He pointed out that many families living in older layouts and smaller houses do not have internal parking facilities and are therefore dependent on roadside parking. He also flagged concerns over residents of rented houses and apartment complexes who may face difficulties under the proposed system. Reddy said the additional annual charge would come at a time when households were already dealing with rising living costs and financial commitments such as education, healthcare, vehicle loans and other expenses. items.title: Better-half will become bitter-half if issues not addressed: Delhi HC acquits man for murder attempt against wife
items.summary: Marriage is paradoxical and a world of extremities, the Delhi High Court recently observed while acquitting a man who was convicted by a trial court for attempting to murder his wife by forcing Baygon Spray (an insecticide) down her throat [Nafe Singh v State] . Justice Vimal Kumar Yadav said that “the best, in no time, becomes worst if not handled carefully”. The Court highlighted recent examples wherein spouses resorted to extreme levels of violence against each other, which was incomprehensible some decades ago. “The better-half becomes the bitter-half if issues are not taken care of and resolved as soon as possible. One of the most beautiful relationships of humans, that is of a husband and wife becomes one of the most terrible when things go wrong in a matrimonial alliance. Time, albeit, is a big healer and tones down a lot of pains in life, however in relationships time taken can also be counterproductive,” the Court stressed. It added that relationships can go in a totally different, undesirable, and unexpected direction if not handled carefully. items.title: Court fees should be refunded to litigants whose cases can't be heard: Madras High Court
items.summary: The Madras High Court recently observed that litigants are “consumers of justice” and they are entitled to a refund of court fees paid if their case cannot be heard because of maintainability [Murugavel Vs Pichai] A Bench of Justices GR Swaminathan and KK Ramakrishnan said that a litigant who mistakenly approaches a court lacking jurisdiction does not receive the service for which the court fee was paid. “Jurist Upendra Baxi would call litigants as consumers of justice. Litigants come to the courts for adjudication of their lis. If the matter could not be taken up for adjudication at all because it was not maintainable in the first instance, the litigant did not receive any service. There has been a failure of consideration and a case for refund stands made out ,” the Court said. Justice GR Swaminathan The Bench made the observation while dealing with an appeal filed by one J Murugavel against an arbitral award passed in October 2024. Murugavel directly challenged the arbitral award before the High Court under Section 37 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996. items.title: Gauhati High Court closes PIL on adjournment reforms after HC notification addresses concerns
items.summary: The Gauhati High Court recently closed a public interest litigation (PIL) petition filed seeking uniform guidelines on adjournments and mandatory digital upload of court records. A Division Bench of Justices Michael Zothankhuma and Arun Dev Choudhury on August 10 noted that the petitioner himself submitted that an intervening administrative notification issued by the High Court Registry had addressed the concerns raised in the matter. "Mr. R. Singh, petitioner-in-person submits that in view of the Notification No. 21 dated 23.03.2026, issued by the Registrar General, Gauhati High Court, nothing survives to be adjudicated in the present Public Interest Litigation (PIL). Accordingly, the instant PIL stands closed," the Court said. Justice Michael Zothankhuma Reetam Singh, an advocate enrolled with the Bar Council of Assam, Nagaland, Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh and Sikkim, had filed the PIL in 2024. He cited his own experience in a case filed under the Negotiable Instruments Act and a money suit to argue that adjournments were being routinely granted by trial courts on inadequate grounds. items.title: Forensic evidence should aid cases, not create more burden for survivors: Ex-ASG Pinky Anand
items.summary: Better forensic practices should strengthen cases before courts without creating an additional burden of proof for survivors of sexual and gender-based violence, former Additional Solicitor General of India Pinky Anand said at a training workshop in Goa on Saturday. The day-long workshop, held on August 22, focused on implementing Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for the collection, preservation, chain of custody and presentation of forensic evidence in cases of sexual assault, rape and child abuse. “Better forensic practice must strengthen the case that reaches the court. It must never become a fresh threshold of belief that survivors are asked to clear,” said Anand. The SOPs were formally launched by Anand at the Police Headquarters in Panjim on April 26 last year, marking World DNA Day. They were subsequently expanded to include the handling of forensic evidence in cases involving child abuse. The workshop brought together police officers, prosecutors, judicial officers, medical practitioners and other professionals involved in the investigation and prosecution of sexual and gender-based violence and child abuse cases.
